name: SikaSeal Super
paste:
SIKASEAL® SUPER: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: SikaSeal® Super, April 2023, Version 01.03 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/w/sikaseal_super_200.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide SikaSeal® Super where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.03).
1.2 Product description. SikaSeal® Super is a one part sealant, designed with all the benefits of a gap sealant and silicone sealant in one.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer.
    - For sealing small indoor connection joints in substrates such as brick, concrete, plaster, ceramics and timber.
    - Small Indoor connection joints around windows, window sills, walls and ceilings etc
    - Suitable for use in kitchens, as well as in most general interior small joint sealing and gap filling applications (with no permanent water immersion)
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.5.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. SikaSeal® Super
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: Multipurpose Gap Sealant
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Approvals, certificates and standards stated by the manufacturer. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (April 2023, Version 01.03) has no approvals, certificates or standards section.
2.3 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - ISO 8339: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Product Information > Modulus of elasticity in tension (p.1); Product Information > Tensile adhesion strength (p.1).
    - ISO 7389: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Product Information > Elastic recovery (p.2).
2.4 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Highly flexible
    - Excellent adhesion properties
    - Mould resistant
    - Paintable* (Felxible paint coatings recommended)
    - Solvent free, water based
    - Easy to apply
    - Water clean-up
    *Due to the flexibility of SikaSeal® Super it is recommended to use a flexible paint coating. Rigid paint coatings may present cracking, crazing or aligatoring of the paint coating system as the substrates move and the sealant flexes.
2.5 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Composition: 1-part acrylic thixotropic paste
    - Colour: White (Dries translucent)
    - Density: 1.0 to 1.2 kg/L
2.6 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Shore A hardness: 45 to 60 (28 days, +23ºC / 50% r.h.)
    - Modulus of elasticity in tension: ~0.6 N/mm2 at 100% elongation (+23°C / 50% r.h.) (ISO 8339)
    - Tensile strain at break: �350%
    - Movement capability: ±20%
    - Tensile adhesion strength: ~1.0 N/mm2 (+23°C / 50% r.h.) (ISO 8339)
    - Elastic recovery: > 90% (+23°C / 50% r.h.) (ISO 7389)
    - Tear strength: ~2.0 N/mm2 (+23°C / 50% r.h.) (DIN 24 method C)
    - Service temperature: Between -30ºC and +80ºC (maximum +40°C in water and temporarily +50°C)
2.7 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: 300 ml cartridge, 12 cartridges per carton
    - Shelf life: 24 months from date of production if stored according to the storage conditions.
2.8 Storage conditions. The product must be stored in undamaged and unopened, original sealed containers, in cool and dry conditions and protected from direct sunlight at temperatures between +5ºC and +25ºC. SikaSeal® Super must be protected from frost.

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.03) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate preparation. The substrate must be sound, clean, dry and free of all contaminants such as dirt, oil, grease, cement laitance, old sealants and poorly bonded paint coatings which could affect adhesion of SikaSeal® Super. The substrate should be of sufficient strength to manage with the stresses induced by the sealant during movement. Removal techniques such as wire brushing, grinding, sanding or other suitable mechanical tools can be used. All dust, loose and friable material must be completely removed from all surfaces before application of SikaSeal® Super.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.03) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Sag flow: �2 mm
    - Curing rate: ~3 mm / 24h (+23ºC / 50% r.h.)
    - Skinning time: ~15 minutes (+23ºC / 50% r.h.)
4.3 Consumption. Joint Design and consumption: For horizontal movement joints, the joint width to depth ratio must be designed to be within the movement capability of the sealant.
    | Joint Width | 5mm | 10mm | 15mm |
    | Joint Depth | 5mm | 8mm | 10mm |
    | Joint Length / | ~10m | ~3.5m | ~2m |
    | 300ml |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
4.4 Application method / tools.
    - Masking: It is recommended to use masking tape where neat or exact joint lines are required. Remove the tape within the skin time after finishing. Application: Prepare the end of the cartridge before or after inserting into the sealant gun then fit the nozzle. Extrude SikaSeal® Super into the joint ensuring that it comes into full contact with the sides of the joint and avoiding any air entrapment.
    - Finishing: As soon as possible after application, sealant must be firmly tooled against the joint sides to ensure adequate adhesion and a smooth finish.Use a compatible tooling agent (e.g. Sika® Tooling Agent N) to smooth the joint surface. Do not use tooling products containing solvents.
4.5 Limitations and important considerations - Limitations.
    - For horizontal gaps with little or no movement the maximum thickness should not exceed 15mm.
    - Maximum vertical joint/gap and depth should not exceed 5mm.
    - Do not use on easy corroding substrates such as blank steel, iron etc.
    - Colour deviations may occur due to chemicals, high temperature, UV radiation. A change in colour ia aesthetic only and does not effect the performance of SikaSeal® Super.
    - Do not use SikaSeal® Super as glass sealer and in joints with permanent water immersion.
    - Do not use on bituminous substrates, natural rubber, chloropene, EPDM or on building materials which might bleed oils, plastisicers or solvent.
    - *Due to the flexibility of SikaSeal® Super it is recommended to use a flexible paint coating. Rigid paint coatings may present cracking, crazing or aligatoring of the paint coating system as the substrates move and the sealant flexes.
4.6 Further information.
    - Safet Data Sheet (SDS).

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Ambient air temperature. +5ºC min / +40ºC max.
5.3 Substrate temperature. +5ºC min / +40ºC max.
5.4 Conditions stated in the limitations. Also stated in the data sheet limitations (clause 4.5):
    - Colour deviations may occur due to chemicals, high temperature, UV radiation. A change in colour ia aesthetic only and does not effect the performance of SikaSeal® Super.
5.5 Test methods printed beside stated values. Each value is as printed in the data sheet with its test method.
    - Modulus of elasticity in tension: ~0.6 N/mm2 at 100% elongation (+23°C / 50% r.h.) (ISO 8339)
    - Tensile adhesion strength: ~1.0 N/mm2 (+23°C / 50% r.h.) (ISO 8339)
    - Elastic recovery: > 90% (+23°C / 50% r.h.) (ISO 7389)
    - Tear strength: ~2.0 N/mm2 (+23°C / 50% r.h.) (DIN 24 method C)
5.6 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.7 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: SikaSeal® Super, April 2023, Version 01.03, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/w/sikaseal_super_200.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: Sikaseal Super, version 18/08/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/r/MSDS%20SikaSeal%20Super%20GHS7.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
